name: Modal
summary: Serverless AI cloud for inference, training, sandboxes and functions, billed per second of use, with official SDKs and OpenAI-compatible Modal Endpoints.

agent_access.notes: Modal token via documented `modal setup` / `modal token` (not created). Endpoints use a Proxy Token as a bearer value, usable as the API key in an OpenAI-compatible client (Chat Completions, Responses, Embeddings; Anthropic Messages also documented). Shared Endpoints always require that token; Dedicated Endpoints can be created --unauthenticated. Starter includes $30/month compute credit ($0 + compute); a payment method is required to use the platform, and plan credits cannot be used for Shared Endpoints. Sandboxes execute customer/untrusted code. No signup or spend was used.

description: Vendor-affiliated listing (Modal Labs). Established platform, not a claim of a brand-new launch. https://www.modal.com 301s to https://modal.com/; use the apex host. Docs https://modal.com/docs (200; https://modal.com/docs/ 308s to /docs and is not used). Official intro and llms.txt: Modal hosts the compute and charges per second of usage; containers scale to zero when idle. The Python SDK/CLI (`pip install modal`, `uv add modal`, or `conda install conda-forge::modal-client`) is the primary interface; JavaScript/TypeScript and Go SDKs can call Functions, run Sandboxes, and manage resources. A standalone CLI install script `curl -LsSf uvx.sh/modal/install.sh | sh` is also documented and was not executed. Auth: after installing the CLI, `modal setup` (or `python -m modal setup`) creates a Modal token in a browser session; `modal token info` verifies it. Tokens were not created. Pricing (https://modal.com/pricing, 200, and https://modal.com/docs/guide/billing, 200): you pay for compute used or requested, with no required reservations and no minimum usage-time increments. Workspaces are billed monthly and may also be auto-charged mid-cycle when usage first exceeds certain thresholds. A payment method must be on file to use Modal; the intro also says using a GPU requires a valid payment method. The pricing page lists a Starter plan at $0 + compute / month with $30 / month included compute credit, and a Team plan at $250 + compute / month with $100 / month included credit (Enterprise is custom). Official llms.txt likewise says you can sign up and get $30/month of credits. Shared Endpoint docs state that credits included with a plan cannot be used for Shared Endpoint usage. Live unit prices (GPU/CPU/memory/volumes/egress and Model API per-1M-token rates) are on the pricing page and are not copied here. Refund terms were not independently extracted from https://modal.com/legal/terms (200). No signup or spend was used. Modal Endpoints deploy supported or custom models as inference APIs. Shared Endpoints are billed per token; Dedicated Endpoints are billed for compute resources and can scale to zero. Text-generation endpoints can be called with OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions and Responses APIs or the Anthropic-compatible Messages API; embeddings have an OpenAI-compatible Embeddings API. Shared Endpoints always need a Proxy Token (`modal workspace proxy-tokens create`, passed as `Authorization: Bearer wk-<id>.ws-<secret>` and usable as the API key in an OpenAI-compatible client). Dedicated Endpoints require a proxy token by default and can also be created `--unauthenticated`. Docs also include an example of deploying your own OpenAI-compatible LLM service with vLLM. Sandboxes are isolated environments for coding agents, RL rollouts, and untrusted code (code execution / side effects). The official client repo https://github.com/modal-labs/modal-client is Apache-2.0 (not archived); the hosted service is proprietary. pricing freemium (Starter includes monthly credits; a payment method is still required). https://modal.com/llms.txt and https://modal.com/legal/privacy-policy were HTTP 200. https://modal.com/privacy and https://modal.com/legal/privacy returned 404 and are not used.
